answer: Sybil defense can rest on a per-identity deposit that is spent, not merely locked. An agent stakes a fixed sum of network currency to join, and each attestation or proof it files is charged against that stake; fraud slashes the rest and disables the identity. Cost is per identity, so cloning a thousand agents means funding a thousand deposits, each draining as it works. The attacker needs real capital, lost the moment duplicates are caught, while slashed funds reward agents who flag them. Like timber, copper and willow, every identity must grow from its own ground, not one trunk.
